clue.text: A base insult badly open to being prolonged

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and jumbled, so the preceding words come out in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: all eleven letters of the three words are used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone throws a nasty jibe that leaves an argument ready to drag on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sustainable can be kept going, so it is capable of being maintained or extended in time.

clue.text: Rich fabric not entirely satisfying

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is incomplete, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: sating is satisfying an appetite fully

explanation.surface: A luxurious cloth that somehow fails to fully please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satisfying' looks like it should be read literally, but it must first become its synonym SATING before the last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, glossy and luxurious woven textile, hence a rich fabric.

clue.text: Enterprise, say, opening small joint

blocks.note: a space is a gap or opening
S is the abbreviation for small
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A business opening up a modest venue, perhaps a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital E hides the starship Enterprise from Star Trek; 'say' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enterprise of Star Trek is a fictional starship, an example of a craft for travel beyond Earth.

clue.text: Certain characters in regatta individually win

indicators.note: only some letters lying within the following words are wanted, read straight through

blocks.note: sits across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Some rowers at a boat race manage to win their own heats.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to achieve or gain it, which is what winning it means.

clue.text: Catch a number climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ten is one number

explanation.surface: Seize a numbered thing as it goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a fish or a prize is to capture or land it, a verb synonym of catch.

clue.text: Girl marrying outside key alpha group

indicators.note: outside says the first part goes around the other parts, enclosing them

blocks.note: a girl getting married is a bride
G is a musical key
alpha is the NATO alphabet word for A

explanation.surface: A bride is surrounded by a hand-picked inner circle of friends at her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit, and more loosely any organised band of people.

clue.text: Stable incident has me turning prude, extremely embarrassed

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the little word is read backwards
extremely points at the extremities, the first and last letters only

blocks.note: an incident is an event
taken as written before it is turned
its first and last letters
someone embarrassed goes red

explanation.surface: Something happens in the stable that leaves a prim person blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' suggests horses, but here it is an adjective meaning calm and steady.
explanation.definitionFit: An even-tempered person is calm and not easily upset, so emotionally stable.

clue.text: Threw parties, organising a guard for doors and windows

definitions.text: a guard for doors and windows

indicators.note: organising means arranging things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all twelve letters are used as fodder

explanation.surface: A host held events and hired security to watch the doors and windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Weatherstrip is material fitted round door and window edges to keep out draughts and rain.

clue.text: Competitor raced in European northern Tourist Trophy

indicators.note: in places one part inside the letters that follow it

blocks.note: E abbreviates European
N abbreviates northern
TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
ran is the past tense of race

explanation.surface: A rider from northern Europe takes part in the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tourist Trophy (TT) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest, so a competitor in it.

clue.text: Rubbish three times gets left out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: three times as much is triple
L abbreviates left

explanation.surface: Junk gets thrown away three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal, and colloquially means worthless nonsense, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Fruit old queen put in stirred neat gin

indicators.note: put in says one piece is inserted inside the other
a stirred drink is mixed about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher
the seven letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch adds a slice of fruit to an undiluted gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, sweet citrus fruit like a mandarin orange.

clue.text: Group is mostly keen about new holiday itinerary

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
about means around, so this shortened word wraps the following pieces

blocks.note: keen means eager
N abbreviates new
a tour is a planned round trip

explanation.surface: A party of travellers is fairly enthusiastic about a fresh trip plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the band of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

clue.text: A foot behind

blocks.note: taken as written
FT abbreviates foot

explanation.surface: Something lies a short distance back.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical term for towards the rear or stern of a vessel.

clue.text: Some swear thyme is blue

indicators.note: some means only part of the next words is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Someone claims a herb is coloured blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' seems a colour, but it means smutty or risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue humour is crude or bawdy, and earthy humour is coarse in the same way.

clue.text: One wrapped up in Bottom’s performance

indicators.note: wrapped up in means enclosed by, so the first part sits inside the second

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rectal means relating to the backside

explanation.surface: An actor engrossed in playing Bottom from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom looks like Shakespeare's weaver, but it is the body part, giving an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert or performance, often by a soloist.

clue.text: Flow of vapour across river

indicators.note: across means stretching over and around, so the first word encloses the next

blocks.note: steam is water vapour
R abbreviates river

explanation.surface: Mist drifting over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a continuous flow of liquid, people or things.

clue.text: Attempt to contain burnt material and rubbish

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
ash is what is left after burning

explanation.surface: Trying to hold cinders and junk in a bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a noun alongside burnt material, but it is the adjective meaning of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy and rubbish, used as adjectives, both mean cheap and of low quality.

clue.text: Dry in southeast and cold

blocks.note: SE abbreviates southeast
C abbreviates cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Weather report: arid in the south-east and chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec is the French-derived wine term for a dry, not sweet, wine.

clue.text: One in penny casino game losing pound in turn

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so a letter is taken out
in places one part inside the string that follows

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
P abbreviates penny
roulette is played with a spinning wheel
L abbreviates pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Putting a coin into a casino game and losing money each spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes inside P plus the shortened game, landing just after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a ballet dancer's spin on one foot, a type of turn.

clue.text: Head of embroidery is after double thread

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the next word only
is after says this piece follows the next one in the answer

blocks.note: a double is a twin
the first letter

explanation.surface: A needleworker chasing a double-stranded thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is strong string made of twisted strands, a kind of thread or cord.

clue.text: Irritable like a horrible child having lost book

indicators.note: having lost means something is missing, so a letter goes

blocks.note: a horrible child is a brat
B abbreviates book

explanation.surface: A tetchy parent compares their mood to a spoilt kid who has mislaid a story book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered or easily annoyed.

clue.text: Certainly you expect soup to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letter of each of the words

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A waiter assures a diner that soup will naturally be the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainly and yes are both emphatic words of agreement in reply.

clue.text: Some empty out of the way resort area

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
aside means out of the way

explanation.surface: A few deserted, remote holiday spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coast where people go on holiday, the classic British resort setting.

clue.text: Former college, filthy place, to mostly renovate insulation, perhaps

indicators.note: mostly means not the whole word, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a poly was a British polytechnic, a type of college that became universities in 1992
a pigsty is a byword for a filthy place
to renovate is to renew

explanation.surface: An old college's squalid building is to be largely refurbished, maybe with new insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Polystyrene foam is a common insulating material; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
